title: DC Open postpones men’s, women’s finals due to rain
content:
WASHINGTON — After nearly nine hours of intermittent heavy rain, thunder and lightning Sunday, the DC Open postponed its women’s and men’s finals until Monday.

Rain delayed the start of the women’s final between the No. 1 seed American Jessica Pegula and rising star Alex Eala of the Philippines by three hours Sunday. Pegula won the first set, 6-4, in smothering humidity and Eala led 2-1 in the second before the rain came again and the tournament suspended play just before 4 p.m.

Pegula and Eala will resume their match at noon Monday. The men’s final between No. 3 seed Taylor Fritz of the United States and the young Spaniard Rafael Jodar will follow.

The tournament announced the postponements at 9:06 p.m. to a hearty few members of the crowd who were still hanging out on the grounds.

The prospect of a Monday final is slightly complicated for the DC Open, which, as a late-summer tournament held in the mid-Atlantic, deals with weather delays nearly every year. But summer storms rarely affect the final in Washington, and extending the tournament by a day puts players in a slight time crunch as the next event on most players’ calendars — the National Bank Open, which hosts its men’s event in Montreal this year and women’s event in Toronto — already started Sunday.

Rain also halted the evening session in both Canadian sites Sunday.

All four finalists in Washington have first-round byes in Canada.
